title: candidate.measured
description: A circuit built from a program was scored by the verifier. The only event that carries a result. Failures are recorded too (passes=false) — a failure plus its reason is the most useful signal a lab assistant can get. Subject is derived as prog:{program}: a candidate has no subject of its own, so history('prog:...') returns the commit and every measurement of it. The candidate's identity is `circuit`; re-measuring a circuit appends another event with the same `circuit`.

program.description: Digest of the program that produced this candidate. Join key to program.committed.

cost.description: The competition cost. LOWER IS BETTER. Always a single scalar, so frontier() works the same across benchmarks. Per benchmark: invsqrt Q x (Toffolis + T/4); dqi R x Q^2 x T (R prices the shot failure rate); dfthcsos lambda x T x Q. Comparable only within the same `cost_basis` and `verifier`.

passes.description: True if the verifier ACCEPTED the circuit. Not 'every shot was correct': some benchmarks (dqi) tolerate a small shot failure rate and charge for it in `cost`, and those circuits pass. Record shot-level error counts in `metrics`. frontier() considers only passing candidates; failing ones stay in the log deliberately.

benchmark.description: Which competition task, e.g. 'invsqrt'. Denormalized from the program for query convenience.

metrics.description: Benchmark-specific numbers. Free-form, so each benchmark adds what it needs with no schema change. invsqrt: {"Q", "T"}. dqi: {"Q", "T", "R", "value_errors", "phase_errors"}. Baseline for reference (invsqrt): Q=260, T=7735, cost=2011100.

circuit.description: SHA-256 of the raw serialized circuit (.kmb/.kmx) — the same bytes the verifier and leaderboard see. This IS the candidate's identity.

config.description: How the program was run to build this circuit: arguments, data files, env. A record for analysing parameter sweeps, NOT a reproducibility guarantee — generators may read inputs this does not capture. Keep small; put anything large in a blob and reference its digest.

rung.description: Which verification tier produced this: conventionally 'smoke' (~1e3 shots), 'screen' (~1e5), or 'full' (~2e8 x 4 seeds). Advisory only — the ladder will change. Judge trustworthiness from `shots` and `seeds`, not from this label.

shots.description: Total shots simulated. Record it consistently on every measurement.

seeds.description: Verifier seeds used. NEVER TRUST A SINGLE SEED. The leaderboard seeds its tests from the circuit's SHA-256 combined with a secret salt, and any edit to a circuit draws a fresh test set, so a candidate passing on one seed may be lucky rather than correct. Nothing should be submitted on fewer than four independent seeds.

verifier.description: Verifier identity and version, e.g. 'kickmix@1.2.0'. Essential: kickmix is migrating to PyPI during this competition, and after an upgrade you must be able to tell which half of your history is still comparable.

cost_basis.description: SEMANTIC TAG: what `cost` actually means, independent of what the field is called. e.g. 'invsqrt/QxC/v1' for Q x (Toffolis + T/4). This is the defence against the worst schema failure — a field keeping its name while its meaning drifts. Two values are comparable only if their cost_basis matches; a consumer that sees two different bases knows it must not compare them, rather than silently producing a confident wrong answer.

failure.description: Present when passes=false. Conventionally {class, first_failing_input, detail}. Free-form — the useful failure taxonomy is not knowable in advance.
